On Wed, Nov 4, 2026 at 14:05 David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com> wrote:
> Team — forwarding BetaPilot's legal ask (attached). Key points summarized: 14-day retention window for request/response logs, evidence of audit fields, and BYOK feasibility for the POC.

Quick technical read:
- We can support a 14-day retention of request/response metadata for a dedicated POC tenant without persisting raw plaintext customer secrets if we do two things: 1) persist only request IDs + response digests + keystore reference IDs (no raw key material), and 2) implement a TTL-based retention pipeline that deletes records after 14 days.
- BYOK for the POC: full BYOK integration (customer-managed HSM with key wrapping) typically requires onboarding that can take weeks. For a quick POC we can do a transient keystore-proxy approach: Redwood issues short-lived wrapping keys and we record keystore reference IDs; BetaPilot still holds HSM ownership for production.
- Concerning audit logs: we'll need to add a few fields to the existing audit schema — keystore_ref, wrapping_key_id, request_id, response_hash, operator_action, and retention_expiry_ts. I sketched a design doc (keystore-proxy-design.md) attached.

Blockers/asks:
- Security: acceptance criteria for the audit fields and whether legal needs hashed vs plain metadata.
- Infra: confirm we can enable TTL deletion pipeline and a scoped POC tenant by Nov 12.

If we aim for Nov 12, infra work must start immediately; I'm happy to lead the keystore-proxy implementation if approved.

—Marissa
Director, Product (Security)
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Short-term retention for BetaPilot POC - legal ask

Thanks for the clear notes — adding compliance perspective:
- Short-term retention of metadata (14 days) is acceptable if we can demonstrate: immutable audit entries for the retention period (i.e., logs cannot be altered, only deleted after TTL) and a deletion proof (a deletion job log showing retention_expiry_ts enforcement).
- Preferred format for evidence: CSV export with request_id, keystore_ref (hashed), action, timestamp, response_hash; plus a signed statement from Redwood security that TTL deletion ran and nights-of-run logs.
- BYOK: for POC we accept the keystore-proxy pattern but Legal requires that the customer signing the POC exception understand that their keys are not fully customer-controlled in the POC — that must be documented in the exception paperwork.
- Required approvals: Security (Irene), Legal (BetaPilot) and Product (Marissa) — then we can route a one-page exception memo for signatures.

Ask to Product/Infra: please draft the acceptance sample (one example CSV row) and a short paragraph describing the deletion proof mechanism by EOD Nov 9 so Legal can approve.

—Irene Choi
Sr. Security Engineer (Compliance Lead)
